City Council Meeting
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
City Council, Community Development Financing Authority, Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*
June 4, 2012
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Ury at 05:01 p.m. , on June 4, 2012, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.
A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by 5:00 p.m. on May 30, 2012, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.
*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."
Present:
Council Member Kelley
Council Member Leckness
Council Member Schlicht
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
Mayor Ury
Absent:
None
Staff Present:
Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager
William P Curley III, City Attorney
Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
Karen Hamman, City Clerk
PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Kelley
INVOCATION: Council Member Leckness
CLOSED SESSION
CS1.
Conference With Legal Counsel - Anticipated Litigation: Initiation of Litigation pursuant to Subdivision (c) of section 54956.9 (two cases).
CS2.
Labor Negotiations - The City Council will Provide Direction to its Labor Negotiator Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6. The Parties to the Negotiations are the City and the City’s Unrepresented Employees. The City’s Negotiator is Dennis Wilberg.
RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE
At the hour of 5:03 p.m., Mayor Ury recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council reconvened at 6:07 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.
REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION
City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council considered two matters regarding initiation of litigation and there was no reportable action. The Personnel matter, item CS2, was not discussed and will be rescheduled at a future meeting.
PRESENTATIONS
P1.
Recognize the Capistrano Valley High School Varsity Boys Swim Team as 2012 CIF Southern Section Division I Champion
Mayor Ury presented certificates of commendation to the CVHS Varsity Boys Swim Team.
PUBLIC COMMENTS
Amanda Bassett, staff member, Lake Forest: speaking on behalf of the American Cancer Society and the Relay for Life planning committee, she thanked the City Council for their continued support of the Relay. She announced that this year’s event raised $105,000 for the American Cancer Society. Michelle Miranda, staff member, Trabuco Canyon: stated that it will be a hardship for her family if her hours are reduced as proposed in the budget item (#16) on tonight’s agenda and she asked that her seniority be considered before a decision is made. Harry Lenczyk, M.V.: stated that dog owners should assist in the construction of a dog park and they should pay to build and maintain it.
Joe Tully, M.V.: expressed his opposition to the proposed Kaleidoscope signage (item 11 on the agenda.)
Gail Reavis, M.V.: asked the City Council to listen to the residents and the cities of Laguna Hills and Laguna Niguel and disapprove the proposed Kaleidoscope signage.
Anna T. Boyce, M.V.: announced that the Marine Adoption Committee is presenting an event for WWII veterans on August 30, 2012, at the Murray Community Center from 11:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. She also announced that the Senior Citizens Advisory Council is holding their monthly meeting at the Community Center on June 8 at 9:00 a.m. and she invited the Council and residents to attend. Lastly she expressed her support for Proposition 29.
F.K. (Joe) Holtzman, M.V.: expressed opposition to Southern California Edison’s smart meter installation and stated that they are not mandatory and residents should opt out. Mr. Holtzman submitted, for the public record, an invitation to a fundraising reception for City Council Candidate Wendy Bucknum and he noted that the host is the same person proposing to place large signs at Kaleidoscope.
Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: read a letter that he wrote to Mayor Ury regarding the OCFA very high fire hazard severity zone maps. He asked the City Council to inform him of the completion status of 6 action items that were assigned to OCFA.
Wendy Bucknum, M.V.: noted that she was honored to be a guest announcer at a dive and swim meet at the Nadadores complex over the weekend. She also expressed her support for local businesses and outlined her attendance at the Relay for Life. She thanked staff for their hard work and stated that she is proud to be a resident of Mission Viejo.
Doreen McKernan, M.V.: expressed her opposition to electronic signs at Kaleidoscope. She also outlined an issue that she is having with the City and the Orange County Sheriff’s Department surrounding the parking permit program. Mrs. McKernan stated that her guests have been unfairly targeted and ticketed.
CONSENT CALENDAR
Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Leckness, to approve the Consent Calendar as described below.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
1.
Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions
Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further reading waived.
2.
City Council Minutes
Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of May 21, 2012, as presented.
3.
Check Register dated May 11, 2012 in the amount of $415,732.95
Ratified the accompanying check register.
4.
Check Register dated May 18, 2012 in the amount of $2,829,786.71
Ratified the accompanying check register.
5.
Requests made by the Mission Viejo Family YMCA for an exemption to the "No Alcoholic Beverage Consumption" Regulation at City facilities.
Approved the request made by the Mission Viejo Family YMCA for an exemption to the "No Alcoholic Beverage Consumption" Regulation for a hosted Mission Viejo Chamber of Commerce mixer.
6.
Marguerite Parkway Median Island Improvements - (CIP 799)
Awarded contract to Marina Landscape, Inc. for the Marguerite Parkway Median Island Improvements in an amount not to exceed $341,690.00.
7.
Renewal of City's Communication Circuit Leases
Approved a three-year agreement with AT&T for $34,950.96 and issue a purchase order for the first year of the agreement in the amount of $11,650.32.
PUBLIC HEARINGS
OLD BUSINESS
The Old Business items were taken out of order.
11.
Request by Colby Durnin of Kaleidoscope that the City Council initiate an Ordinance amending the City’s sign regulations to create a new sign district with allowance for electronic signs and off-site advertising for Kaleidoscope and possibly a larger area
Director of Community Development Chuck Wilson presented the staff report.
Colby Durnin, Kaleidoscope Center: outlined his request to amend the City’s sign regulations and to create a sign district. He also displayed visual renditions of the type of signs that he is proposing for Kaleidoscope.
The following spoke in opposition to the proposed signage and a sign district: Harry Lenczyk, M.V.; Larry Gilbert, M.V.; Melody Carruth, Mayor of the City of Laguna Hills; Millie Summerlin, M.V.; G.E. Brown, M.V.; Mark Sierakowski, M.V.; Matt Corrigan, M.V.; Maggie Merante, General Manager of the Nellie Gail Ranch Homeowner’s Association, Laguna Hills; Dierdre Spalding, Member of the Nellie Gail Ranch Owners Association, Laguna Hills; Paul Drysch, Laguna Hills; Dale Tyler, M.V.; Ed Sachs, M.V.; Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.; Bob Bruchmann, M.V.; and Doreen McKernan, M.V.
The following spoke in support of the proposal: Reed L. Royalty, San Juan Capistrano, President of the Orange County Taxpayers Association; Jim Leach, CEO of the South Orange County Regional Chamber and Economic Coalition; Curt Stanley, Rancho Santa Margarita, member of the Chambers of Commerce and the Economic Coalition; Ron James, M.V.; Dennis O’Connor, M.V., Member of the South Orange County Economic Development Committee; Matthew Dragas, Aliso Viejo, owner of Buffalo Wild Wings, M.V.; and David Russell Ohrn, Laguna Woods.
Colby Durnin, Kaleidoscope Center: provided additional information on the proposal in response to comments made by members of the public.
Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Leckness, to reject the draft sign ordinance submitted by Colby Durnin and direct staff to return with various options and standards for exterior signage which may or may not include a sign district.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
Council Member Schlicht, and Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
ABSENT:
None
RECESS
At the hour of 9:36 p.m., Mayor Ury declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 9:50 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.
8.
Landscape Improvements to Casta Del Sol Road
Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.
Council Member Leckness departed the room at 9:53 p.m. and returned at 9:55 p.m.
Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, to (1) approve Contract Amendment No. 2 to Mariposa Landscapes Inc. in an amount not to exceed $111,400; and (2) approve Contract Amendment No. 2 to S. Parker Engineering, Inc. in an amount not to exceed $36,600.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Leckness, Mayor Ury, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, Council Member Schlicht, and Council Member Kelley
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
9.
Marguerite Tennis Center Renovation Project (CIP 501)
Kelly Doyle, Director of Recreation and Community Services, outlined the reasons for the proposed change order.
Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, to approve Change Order No. 2 for Construction Management Services with Friess Construction, Inc. in an amount not to exceed $22,000.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
Council Member Schlicht
ABSENT:
None
10.
Agreement for Professional Services Among the Successor Agency of Community Development Agency of the City of Mission Viejo, and the Mission Viejo Housing Authority, and the City of Mission Viejo, and The Davis Company for Special Economic Consulting Services
City Manager Dennis Wilberg presented the staff report.
Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, to free form to approve the Professional Services Agreement with The Davis Company for Special Economic Consulting Services.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
NEW BUSINESS
ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR
MAYOR'S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS
12.
Use of the Thomas R. Potocki Conference Center for the School Year 2012- 2013 from September 2012 through mid-June 2013.
Scott Ramirez, Rancho Santa Margarita: thanked the City Council for supporting the Outta Bounds program at the Potocki Center and stated that ultimately he would like to see the facility used as an all-inclusive youth center.
Motion made by , seconded by , to
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
13.
Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report
Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: reported on the May 24, 2012, OCFA Board Meeting and the board’s action to conduct an investigation into the possibility of Workers Compensation fraud. He also discussed OCFA’s decision to not seek competitive bids for a broker/dealer contract.
Council Member Kelley presented the report.
14.
Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report
Mayor Ury presented the report.
15.
San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon presented the report.
STAFF REPORTS
City Manager’s Report
16.
Adoption of the Revised FY 2012-13 City Operating and Capital Improvement Program Budget
City Manager Dennis Wilberg and Director of Administrative Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report and answered questions.
Motion made by , seconded by , to
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
17.
Report on Recent Actions of the Successor Agency Oversight Board
City Manager Wilberg presented the report and highlighted that the State has approved the recognized obligation payment schedule but it does not include the $1.2 million in right-of-way for the Watermarke project.
City Attorney’s Report
18.
Ordinance Repealing the Requirement that City Contractors Use the E-Verify Program
Motion made by , seconded by , to
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
Council Member Schlicht announced that she has received complaints from Palmia residents regarding the demolition of the former K-Mart building and she asked the City Attorney for input.
City Attorney Curley responded that in general, the CEQA process is complete. The city has health and safety requirements in its building codes which would have been adhered-to during the demolition process and the City’s inspections.
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon outlined her correspondence with the Community Development department and noted that she did not observe any dust when she recently drove by the project at night.
City Manager Wilberg announced that staff has followed-up on complaints from residents and will continue to monitor the project.
COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS
19.
Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended
The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.
Council Member Kelley
Council Member Kelley reported on her trip to the International Council of Shopping Centers conference (ICSC) where she gathered good ideas and information. She noted that she was advised to post a listing of available commercial space and sites for sale on the City’s web site along with the good news regarding business activity. She also announced that there are 8 new restaurants that have opened recently or will be opening soon in Mission Viejo. Council Member Kelley outlined her attendance at the City’s Memorial Day service and the Relay for Life. She invited residents to donate blood on June 15, 2012, from 12:30 to 6:30 p.m. at city hall in the Saddleback room. Interested parties can sign up on-line or call her for an appointment. Council Member Kelley congratulated the Capistrano Valley High School Varsity Boys Swim Team for winning the 2012 CIF Southern Section Division I Championship. She noted that there are so many great schools and talented athletes in the City of Mission Viejo. Lastly, Council Member Kelley announced that she and Council Member Leckness would like to provide a report, at the next City Council Meeting, on the recent meeting of the CUSD ad hoc committee.
Council Member Leckness
Council Member Leckness outlined his attendance at recent events including the KSBR Jazz Festival, the Memorial Day ceremony, the Dreadnaughts at War program, and the Relay for Life.
Council Member Schlicht
Council Member Schlicht discussed her attendance at a very uplifting memorial ceremony for Tom Fuentes. She noted that she too attended the City’s Memorial Day event which is always very poignant and she asked that the American Legion be included in future ceremonies. Council Member Schlicht reminded residents to vote in the election tomorrow and she quoted Congressman Dana Rohrabacher with “the lowest level of activism is to vote.” She also announced that residents in the El Toro Water District can send a letter, by June 28, 2012, to the district office to protest increased water rates. Lastly, Council Member Schlicht invited residents to provide input on the housing element of the City’s General Plan by attending one of two workshops which will be held on Thursday, June 7 at 10:00 a.m. and at 6:00 p.m.
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon announced that she was unable to attend the Memorial Day ceremony but she heard from friends that it was a very solemn and profoundly significant event. Although she wasn’t present on Memorial Day, she did bring her grandsons to the Kershaw Garden to walk through and view the American Heroes tribute banners and she thanked Assistant City Manager Keith Rattay for his work to display the banners. Mayor Pro Tem Reardon outlined her attendance at the Relay for life and she expressed her appreciation to the staff members who are involved each year. She also discussed her attendance at the Disneyland Scholarship program and she noted that award of the scholarships is based on service rather than academics. She was pleased to see Mission Viejo resident and Capistrano Valley High School student Michael Tompkins receive an award for completing 910 volunteer hours in 2011. Mayor Pro Tem Reardon summarized her attendance the Orange County Sheriff’s Department regional training academy and the Ladera Rancho Chamber of Commerce meeting where she heard an update on the Ranch development. Lastly, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon invited residents to see the screening of a very important movie on accidental prescription drug overdoses called “Overtaken.” The family event will be held on Thursday, June 7 from 6:30 to 8:30 p.m. at the Kaleidoscope center.
Mayor Ury
Mayor Ury reiterated previous comments on the City’s very special Memorial Day Ceremony and the Relay for Life event.
ADJOURNMENT
At the hour of 11:01 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session, Mayor Ury adjourned the meeting to Monday, June 18, 2012, at 5:00 p.m.
______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk
Approved at the meeting of June 18, 2012
